item.title: Bijan Robinson Tells Recruits To Ignore NIL Cash For 40-Year Future
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Bijan Robinson is telling young athletes to stop chasing the biggest check and start looking at the whole picture. The Falcons running back knows exactly what it takes to make it, and he is not happy with the current mindset in college recruiting. He warns that cash is pulling kids away from the coaches who actually care about their future. This is not just advice for high schoolers; it is a warning for the entire league. The Distraction of Quick Cash Robinson played high school football before the name, image, and likeness era took over the sports world. He sees a major problem today where athletes pick schools based on the payout rather than the plan. “I think money has been very much of a distraction for kids,” Robinson said in an interview with Sports Illustrated . He believes players are ignoring the relationships that help them grow. If a recruit spends all their time counting dollars instead of talking to coaches, they are making a huge mistake. The money comes and goes, but the right mentor stays with you forever. He remembers his own path from Tucson to Texas. He did not think he needed to go to a big school to get noticed, but he was wrong. Arizona offered him a scholarship after just five varsity games. More offers came later, and he realized the coaches were coming to him. He did not have to chase the money to get the chance. He just had to be ready when the right people showed up. Thinking Four Decades Ahead The most important lesson Robinson learned came from his former high school coach, Dennis Bene. The two talked about life after football long before Robinson ever stepped on an NFL field. Bene taught him to look past the next three years of college ball. “The decision I was making was not just gonna be for a three-year decision, but gonna be for a 40-year decision,” Robinson recalled. That shift in thinking changed everything for him. It is about building a life that lasts, not just a season that ends in May. Bene was more than a coach to Robinson; he was a father figure who checked on his life off the field too. “Not only was he just a father figure for me, but he was a guy that always just made sure that I was doing great things off the field and on the field,” Robinson said. That kind of support is rare, and it is exactly what kids need to hear now. Chasing a NIL deal might pay for a new car, but a good coach pays for a future. Proof That the Work Pays Off Robinson is living proof that his advice works. He is putting up MVP numbers this season for the Falcons, even with a shaky team start. Yahoo Sports reports that over seven games, he has accumulated 704 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 131 carries. He also has 25 receptions for 203 yards and one more touchdown. His total yards from scrimmage sit at 907, and he is averaging 129.6 yards per game. That is elite production, and it did not come from picking the school with the most cash. item.title: Josh Simmons reportedly asked to leave meeting by Patrick Mahomes, Andy Reid
item.description: Former Ohio State offensive lineman Josh Simmons was asked to leave a Kansas City Chiefs team meeting by quarterback Patrick Mahomes and head coach Andy Reid, according to NFL Network insiders Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo . "There are a lot of questions about Josh Simmons, who is as talented as a left tackle as you can possibly get," Rappaport said. "He is a stud as a player. I don't know if he plays for the Chiefs again. I don't know when he plays for the Chiefs again." Those comments aired on ESPN's "Big Day with Peter Schrager," Oct. 27. Per the initial report , published on Oct. 25, Simmons was sitting with his feet up in the offense's meeting room when Reid asked Simmons to put his feet down. Simmons pushed back, saying he had to sit that way due to back and hip pain, so Reid told Simmons to leave and get treatment, which Mahomes echoed. Simmons apologized to Reid and team leadership later in the day, telling them he could've handled the situation better, according to the report. Simmons has yet to play for the Chiefs this season due to a bulging disc in his back. He returned to practice during the Chiefs' Week 5 off week, but missed practice on Oct. 25, with the Chiefs listing his absence as "back/not injury related-personal." According to the report, the incident in the meeting room occurred that same day. The Chiefs placed Simmons on injured reserve on Oct. 26. The earliest he can return is Week 11 of the NFL season. The Chiefs selected Simmons with the 32nd overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. He played in eight games his rookie year. After missing a chunk of games due to family/personal reasons, Simmons then dislocated and fractured his wrist against the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. He underwent surgery and missed the rest of the season. "I don't know if he plays for the Chiefs again." - @RapSheet on Josh Simmons on @BigDayESPN pic.twitter.com/wLp5Ot2aBb — Peter Schrager (@PSchrags) October 27, 2026 Simmons transferred to the Buckeyes after his sophomore year with San Diego State. Before Ohio State won the national championship during Simmons' senior year, he tore his patellar tendon when the Buckeyes lost to Oregon on Oct. 12, 2024. item.description: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images Austin Smotherman has officially turned the fall season into his personal playground. Having gone 99 times without a PGA Tour win, the 32-year-old has now secured two victories within 101 career starts. This rapid turnaround began at the Bank of Utah Championship and concluded on Monday morning in Bermuda. The win at the Butterfield Bermuda Championship was not just a career milestone; it was a statement made under pressure and high winds at Port Royal Golf Course. The path to the trophy was complicated by weather. High winds forced the cancellation of Sunday’s final round, reducing the tournament to 54 holes. According to the Fulton Sun, Smotherman and Seamus Power finished regulation play level on 16-under par, requiring a sudden-death playoff to decide the champion. Monday morning saw the two competitors return, where they both recorded pars on their initial two trips to the par-three 16th hole. The drama ended on the third extra hole when Smotherman secured the title with another par. Because Power missed the green, he could not salvage par from the rough; his chip reached 16 feet, yet the putt was missed. Golf Retailing reports that Smotherman defeated Power in an all-Titleist Pro V1x playoff, marking the 29th PGA Tour victory of the year for a player using their golf balls. Smotherman carded rounds of 65, 66, and 66 during the event, recording 17 birdies and an eagle. Power reached the same total score with rounds of 66, 64, and 67. The leaderboard clearly showed dominance, with Titleist ball players filling the first nine spots. Sixteen players utilized the next-generation balls in Bermuda while the brand extended its validation programme across the professional tours. item.title: Brewers manager Pat Murphy recalls heart attack scare, ponders a new tattoo
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL — Pat Murphy has been thinking about getting a new tattoo and he's been looking for inspiration on what kind to get. He may have found it. In his pregame press conference Tuesday afternoon, Oct. 27, before Game 4 of the World Series, the Milwaukee Brewers manager was asked about surviving a heart attack six years ago. More: Brewers bench coach Pat Murphy on surviving a heart attack and getting a second chance And Murph being Murph, launched into a story. "I swore I wasn't having a heart attack. The ambulance driver, wherever he is, the ambulance driver out there that was in the back of the ambulance that day, I apologize," Murphy began. "It's the first time I've apologized on the record because this ambulance driver was like, ' sir, can I have your next of kin?' "I'm like, bro, next of kin? I'm not going anywhere. You don't need to know my next of kin. OK? 'Would you like to donate your organs?' "I'm like are you (expletive) me? Did you just ask me that? "I showed him pictures of my kids. 'I don't know about you, but I ain't going anywhere. Just chill down on that thing.'" Murphy suffered the heart attack Aug. 2, 2020, during a Brewers workout, when he was the bench coach. Murphy continued the story from his point of view on the incident with the paramedic. "He was like dead serious. He was like super ripping my shirt off. They're sticking stuff on me. I was making them laugh," said Murphy. "Our trainer was there, Scott Barringer at the time, and he was white as a ghost. He didn't know what to think. I'm just joking with the guy like what are we doing here? "Then I got in the room, and all these people are lined up with these white coats on and gloves. And I said, you people are way too serious right now. Whatever you got going on, let's chill out a little bit. This is going to be fine. I'm doing good. "That's the last I remember. I think they shot something in my IV, and that was it." It was a philosophical moment for the 67-year-old coach. "Yeah, I don't know if it changed me at all. It always does when you think about the seriousness of when you're raising kids, you know what I mean? I got two young ones so I can't go anywhere yet," said Murphy. "When those two young ones are at a little better stage, I can shut the curtain. "The perspective is always there. Remember, 'man you were dust and to dust you shall return.' All us Catholics we've heard that. I actually might get that as a tattoo. What do you think? "I was thinking about getting a tattoo for the season, and that could be a good one. 2026, remember, man, you're dust and to dust you shall return." item.title: Canelo vs Mbilli: Start time, undercard and how to watch fight this weekend
item.description: Canelo Alvarez will return to the ring this weekend, challenging Christian Mbilli for the WBC super-middleweight title in Riyadh . Although the Saudi city has been the target of deadly attacks in recent weeks , Canelo has arrived ahead of his first fight in 13 months , after he was outpointed by fellow great Terence Crawford in Las Vegas. Against Mbilli, the 36-year-old Canelo faces a stern task; the Cameroonian is the younger man, at 31, and he enters his first title defence with an unbeaten record. Canelo Alvarez (right) at the weigh-in for his fight with Terence Crawford (Getty) Last time out, on the Canelo vs Crawford undercard, Mbilli fought Lester Martinez to a brutal draw to retain the interim WBC title, but he was later upgraded to regular champion when Crawford retired. Can Canelo prove that he is still among the best in the world? Or, as he returns from elbow surgery, will he show himself to be in the twilight of his great career? Here’s all you need to know. When is the fight? Canelo vs Mbilli will take place on Saturday 31 October at the ANB Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The main card is expected to begin at 6pm GMT (11am PT / 1pm CT / 2pm ET), with main-event ring walks following at 8.30pm GMT (1.30pm PT / 3.30pm CT / 4.30pm ET). How can I watch it? The event will stream live exclusively on DAZN pay-per-view at a cost of £24.99 ($79.99 in the US), and on DAZN Ultimate Tier – which is priced at £24.99 per month. You can purchase the fight or an Ultimate Tier subscription here. Will the event go ahead, and why is this a question? The organisation of the fight card has been the subject of intense speculation in recent weeks, due to numerous deadly attacks on Riyadh’s airports. The international airport has reopened, but the US Department of State has urged citizens to “reconsider travel to Saudi Arabia due to risk of drone and missile targeting", while areas near the Yemen border have been listed as such: “do not travel due to terrorism”. item.title: Posada Says Yankees Don’t Want Him Back And He Is Right
item.description: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Jorge Posada does not feel welcome back at the Yankees. He told The New York Post on Tuesday that he believes the organization does not want him there. The five-time World Series champion played his entire 17-year career in The Bronx. Despite his legacy, he says he will not return to help the team because he feels shut out. Posada spoke to reporters Joel Sherman and Jon Heyman on “The Show” podcast. He said he could help, but he doubts the team wants him. “It’s gotta be the right — I mean, I could, but I don’t think they want me there to tell you the truth,” Posada said. This is a sharp break for a man who won five titles with the club. The 2011 Fallout Still Hurts The reason for this distance goes back to his final season. Posada played his last year in 2011. That season was rough for both him and the front office. He was moved from catcher to a part-time designated hitter. He feuded with management over his playing time. “My last season of my career was a really tough one when it comes to handling everything on my part and also the Yankees toward Jorge Posada,” he said. He noted that he never got a chance to fight for his job. According to him, the front office issued the directive rather than then-manager Joe Girardi. While conversing with Girardi, he clarified that he reached out to neither owner Hal Steinbrenner nor general manager Brian Cashman. He said, “I don’t know what happened. I’d rather just move forward.” That pain from 2011 still stops him from walking into spring training today. He described the feeling of going to the stadium now. “I don’t feel welcome when I go there, you know?” Even during spring training, I do not feel like — I am simply like, I do not know, I do not feel welcome. Since I believe they do not want me there, I choose not to go. A legend who gave everything to the team now feels like an outsider in his own home. He Wants Accountability But Not the Job Posada still cares about the team. He thinks the Yankees need a strong voice to push players. He wants higher standards of accountability. He said mental mistakes get magnified during the playoffs. “You didn’t run to first base?” Get him out of the game. Make him understand that this means something. This is really a job, not a game, and certain guys are failing to do their job. He wants someone to say that certain plays are unacceptable. However, he does not blame the current leadership. He said general manager Brian Cashman and manager Aaron Boone are the right people to lead. item.title: Arsenal stunned by fourth-tier Fleetwood as underdogs win shoot-out
item.description: Fleetwood Town's Aaron Loupalo-Bi (2nd L) celebrates scoring his side's first goal during the English Carabao Cup fourth round soccer match between Fleetwood Town and Arsenal at Highbury Stadium. (is associated with: «Arsenal stunned by fourth-tier Fleetwood as underdogs win shoot-out») Nick Potts/PA Wire/dpa Fourth-division Fleetwood shocked Premier League champions Arsenal in a penalty shoot-out to advance to the League Cup quarter-finals after a 1-1 draw on Tuesday. Bruno Guimaraes saw his spot-kick saved by Jay Lynch before Fleetwood's teenage defender Conor Haughey lashed home an emphatic penalty. It sparked a pitch invasion at Highbury Stadium as hosts Fleetwood triumphed 5-3 in one of the greatest upsets in the competition's history. Fleetwood, 18th in the fourth tier, dared to dream after Fulham loanee Aaron Loupalo-Bi put them in front after 21 minutes against a much-changed Arsenal side struggling to find any fluidity on the North West coast. The half-time introduction of Martin Odegaard changed the game as the Gunners looked much improved after the break, drawing level in the 50th minute when Viktor Gyokeres just about managed to turn in his first goal of the season. But as Arsenal turned up the heat without reward, their frustration boiled over as their teenage prodigy Max Dowman was sent off with five minutes left to play. There was still time for Lynch to make huge saves from Ben White and Odegaard before it went to a shoot-out in which Fleetwood were perfect from the spot to secure a historic win. Bradford are through to the League Cup quarter-finals for the first time since they reached Wembley in 2013 with a 2-0 win over Peterborough.

The San Francisco 49ers announced additional roster moves Tuesday after reacquiring three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner from the Indianapolis Colts ahead of the NFL trade deadline. San Francisco signed defensive lineman Kevin Givens to its practice squad and released wide receiver Malik Turner from the practice squad as the organization continued adjusting its roster following the blockbuster trade. Buckner spent his first four NFL seasons with San Francisco before the 49ers traded him to Indianapolis in 2020 for a first-round selection . San Francisco’s latest roster adjustments follow Sunday’s disappointing 29-20 loss to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7 . The defeat ended the 49ers’ undefeated start and dropped them to 6-1, although they remain among the NFC’s top contenders. Adding Buckner provides San Francisco with an experienced interior defensive lineman as the team attempts to regain momentum following its first setback. item.title: Why the state of Texas has no sure things for College Football Playoff
item.description: UTSA Roadrunners head coach Jeff Traylor after the game against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) I knew dang near nothing, and proved it. Way back in August, when the email inbox delivered an assignment to make a bunch of college football predictions with fellow Hearst newspaper columnists from around the state, there was little doubt this would end badly. While my esteemed, ever-conscientious colleagues in Austin and Dallas and Houston had been poring over transfer-portal rankings and evaluating preseason practice reports, I'd pretty much had my feet up after following the local cagers through the NBA Finals. As it turned out, a catch-up cram session didn't help much. I picked a national champion that's already lost three times and fallen out of the Top 25, and a national runner-up that lost to BYU , and a Heisman Trophy winner who underperformed before suffering an injury from which he's not likely to return this season. But when it came time to predict how many teams from Texas – a state loaded in the preseason with supposed championship contenders – might make the College Football Playoff? Without a good answer, my instinct was to ask what seemed like a preposterous question: "What if it's zero?" A couple of months later, that question still applies. Texas, which climbed as high as No. 1 in September, still is hanging around the playoff conversation after treating a run of double-digit leads the way the Spurs did in the NBA Finals, but the Longhorns don't inspire much confidence. After two meltdowns against unranked opponents, Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning and Texas' vaunted artificial intelligence apparatus still have trips to Missouri, LSU and Texas A&M on the schedule. Maybe they can get in with a third loss. But it wouldn't be a surprise to see them suffer a fourth one. If the Longhorns need a reason to be optimistic, one might be that the only real resistance the Aggies have put up this season has been against their most dedicated message-board posters . Coach Mike Elko later apologized for referring to the TexAgs online community as a "cesspool." But it's probably wise not to specify what part of a house's plumbing infrastructure that 15 th place in the Southeastern Conference represents. The Aggies are out of the playoff running, and the only race that Baylor and TCU have left over the next month is the one to get mentioned in the most internet articles speculating about trying to hire UTSA's Jeff Traylor. item.title: Xabi Alonso’s return to Liverpool felt inevitable – behind the scenes, the reality was always different
item.description: A wonderful long passer and a midfielder with the capacity to score from the halfway line, Xabi Alonso always seemed to have the ability to plot the way to a far-off target with expert precision. For years, the theory was that it would transport the former Liverpool midfielder to the dugouts at Anfield. When it has, though, it has been the opposition technical area: first with Bayer Leverkusen , then Real Madrid , the other club with whom he won the Champions League, now with Chelsea , the club beaten on Merseyside in two Champions League semi-finals two decades ago. A man who created many a Liverpool goal has promised he will celebrate “for sure” if Chelsea score at Anfield on Wednesday; he had nothing to celebrate in 2024, however, when his Leverkusen were walloped 4-0 , or last year, when his Real lost 1-0 . Alonso has returned to Anfield with Bayer Leverkusen and Real Madrid but coming back with Chelsea for the Carabao Cup fourth round will bring a different atmosphere (Getty) The chant in Alonso’s playing days, when Liverpool represented the ancien regime and Chelsea the nouveau riche , was that the Londoners “ain’t got no history”. Liverpool and Alonso have plenty; he scored their first goal against AC Milan in “the miracle of Istanbul”, and they spiralled into decline after his 2009 sale to Real. When he took Leverkusen to an unbeaten double, he looked a Liverpool manager in waiting. Now the wait may be never-ending. When Jurgen Klopp announced in January 2024 that he would stand down, Alonso seemed the best candidate. Including, it soon transpired, to Klopp himself, who appeared to give the Basque his blessing as his successor. Describing managers of his vintage as dinosaurs, the German said: “The next generation is already there and I would say Xabi is standout.” Whether or not the Liverpool hierarchy at the time concurred, they were soon deterred. While Bayern Munich mounted a public chase of Alonso, Liverpool did not. “At that time, I was at Leverkusen and I was aware of the situation but I decided to stay,” he said. He never spoke to Liverpool. The greater surprise, perhaps, was that he did not in 2026, either. Two years ago, after Ruben Amorim was wrongly described as the frontrunner, Arne Slot was instead appointed. Slot won a Premier League title while Madrid, the third superclub Alonso represented, hired him a year later. Yet his sacking by Real in January felt like a case of bad timing for an increasingly beleaguered Slot . Alonso’s sudden availability made him the obvious alternative, the king over the water. The idea of Alonso was seductive to many a Liverpool fan, if not to their hierarchy. They did not intervene when Chelsea made their move for a man who once had his ankle broken by Frank Lampard in one of the many flashpoints of a rivalry that had a bitterness when Rafa Benitez and Jose Mourinho patrolled the technical areas. Alonso became a great at Anfield while Liverpool’s rivalry with Chelsea peaked on the pitch (Getty)

item.title: Barcelona star Lamine Yamal issues official response to missing out on Ballon d’Or
item.description: Barcelona star Lamine Yamal issues official response to missing out on Ballon d’Or Barcelona star Lamine Yamal has on Tuesday taken to social media, to issue an official response to missing out on the Ballon d’Or award. Attacker Lamine was of course in attendance yesterday evening, as the Ballon d’Or gala was held in front of a packed crowd at the London Palladium. The 19-year-old was considered to be amongst the very frontrunners for the accolade, after a spectacular year culminating in glory in both La Liga and at the World Cup. item.title: Arsenal stunned by fourth-tier Fleetwood in League Cup
item.description: Fleetwood striker Aaron Loupalo-Bi celebrates scoring against Arsenal (Darren Staples) Arsenal suffered one of the most humiliating defeats in their history as the Premier League champions were stunned by fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in a League Cup penalty shoot-out on Tuesday. Mikel Arteta's side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time. Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes had his penalty saved by Jay Lynch in the shoot-out and Conor Haughey scored Fleetwood's winner. Aaron Loupalo-Bi's first-half goal had put Fleetwood ahead before Viktor Gyokeres equalised after the interval. Arsenal's 16-year-old rising star Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct in the closing stages. Arteta paid the price for prioritising Sunday's Premier League trip to Liverpool as his decision to make nine changes backfired spectacularly. No one would have predicted Arsenal's embarrassment regardless of Arteta's selection gamble. They had moved level on points with Premier League leaders Manchester City after a 2-0 victory over Everton on Saturday. But instead of extending their run of 11 wins from their 13 previous games, Arsenal returned to north London red-faced after a loss that ranks among the darkest days in the club's glittering history. Arsene Wenger's Arsenal suffered a shock League Cup loss against fourth tier Bradford on penalties in 2012. Arteta's team were beaten by second tier Southampton in the FA Cup last season and also lost to Nottingham Forest, then in the Championship, in the same competition in 2022. Supporters of an older vintage will recall Arsenal's 1969 League Cup final loss against third tier Swindon and their 1992 FA Cup exit at fourth tier Wrexham. But even those painful defeats cannot compare to this remarkable result. For once, Arsenal fans will not have fond memories of Highbury -- Fleetwood's ground shares the same name as the Gunners' ancestral home before their move to the Emirates Stadium in 2006. Fleetwood's tiny 5,327-capacity ground -- where goals are celebrated with a burst of children' cartoon song Captain Pugwash over the tannoy -- is a far cry from the famous marble halls and dignified grandeur of Arsenal's former stadium. Now it will be remembered forever as the site of Arsenal's most chastening loss in the Arteta era. Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor wept tears of joy as disbelieving fans flooded the pitch to celebrate their club's astonishing victory. - 'Cod Army' uprising - Only Myles Lewis-Skelly and Viktor Gyokeres kept their places from the Everton game, with teenagers Dowman and Marli Salmon starting, while 18-year-old winger Ceadach O'Neill made his debut. item.title: Super Bowl-Winning QB Urges Minnesota Vikings to Make Blockbuster Trade for $44M Pro Bowler
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Vikings are the last undefeated team left, and general manager Nolan Teasley has surely been busy working the trade lines as he navigates his first trade deadline in an enviable position. Will the Vikings capitalize on their hot start? The belief is the Vikings will be making a move of some kind before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, and a former Super Bowl-winning quarterback knows exactly who Kevin O’Connell’s team should be targeting. Related: 6-Step Plan to Build 6-0 Minnesota Vikings Into Super Bowl Champions Russell Wilson Wants Minnesota Vikings to Add Jonathan Taylor to Unleash Kyler Murray and Justin Jefferson Oct 25, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) rushes the ball against the Minnesota Vikings in the first half at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Rempel-Imagn Images The Vikings could address a number of needs, from the interior offensive line, a blocking tight end, another pass-rushing DT, a rotational edge rusher, or a safety to further strengthen the NFL’s best defense. Yet, the better approach may be to add a difference-maker who can unlock the potential within coach O’Connell’s offense, and the perfect target may or may not be available. Appearing on CBS’ “ Set Hut ” alongside Chris Long, former Super Bowl-winning quarterback Russell Wilson urged the Vikings to get aggressive and trade for Jonathan Taylor . “Maybe we knock on the door of Jonathan Taylor and see if we can get that running game going with Aaron Jones and have a two-tandem running back system. He’s got 140 rushes already, 587 yards, this is just this season. You know who knows how to score touchdowns? This guy knows how to score touchdowns, he’s got eight of ’em already and Daniel Jones isn’t playing good in Indy.” Russell Wilson on Jonathan Taylor Trade to Vikings The First-Team All-Pro would give the Vikings one of the best running backs in the NFL, whose combined speed, power, and excellent vision to record at least 1,000 yards from scrimmage in five of the past six seasons. It’s also Wilson’s belief that the three-time Pro Bowl running back would make life easier for Murray and even Justin Jefferson, opening up more opportunities downfield, with the front seven keying in on trying to slow down Taylor too. “What could he do if you gave Kyler Murray a running back? Let him put under center, downhill runs, play-action. Get the ball deep down the field. Justin Jefferson needs to have at least a go ball a quarter. We gotta be throwing the ball to him no matter what. If there’s two guys on him, still, throw it to him, it’s a him route, it doesn’t matter, but when you got a guy like this, it makes it a one-high defense, 1-on-1 matchups for Justin Jefferson.” Wilson on How Taylor Trade Would Impact Vikings Trade matchmaker @DangeRussWilson believes Jonathan Taylor could be the missing ingredient for the Vikings offense 👀 #SetHut https://t.co/c6ObMTb4qo — NFL on CBS 🏈

item.title: Michael Penix Jr., Pat Mahomes, and 2 More Must-Sit Quarterbacks in Week 8 Fantasy Football
item.description: Oct 25, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) makes a throw against the San Francisco 49ers during the fourth quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. It is a tough, unpredictable game, for that matter. That brings me to an extensive statistical analysis that labels the following four quarterbacks as benchable in Week 8. Baker Mayfield The intrigue is well-placed following a 43-point win after Week 7. But Mayfield is not startable. He played in Week 7 with gloves on, which he said would affect his grip and his throwing mechanics, and it contributed to him throwing the ball only 11 times. The thumb injury will linger all year. item.description: French pro footballer Kylian Mbappé has become controversial in China after a clip of him referring to a "Chinese dictator" went viral over the last day. The dictator in question is Mao Zedong, leading multiple Chinese brands to drop Mbappé’s deals with them. Mbappé has since issued an apology to China and the Chinese people as the controversy surrounding the incident continues generating discourse online. Soccer star Kylian Mbappé is famous for representing France internationally, including winning the 2018 FIFA World Cup for his country. He has consistently scored for France in the two World Cup editions that followed, as well as in other international tournaments, and captains France’s National Soccer Team since 2023. He has also become a notable player for France’s Paris Saint-Germain and Spain’s Real Madrid, the latter of which is his current club. However, the renowned athlete found himself at the center of a controversy in China for an answer he gave during an interview with The Bridge, a French talk show, in a short clip that was posted to its social media, and which they have since deleted. In the clip, Mbappé talks about a version of the popular "Dictator Mbappé" meme, which depicts him as a Chinese dictator, among other dictator-like personas. 😂🇫🇷 Kylian Mbappé avoue qu’il rigole en voyant les memes qui le représentent en… dictateur. 😭 @Thebridge_show #Mbappé #Football #Memes #France https://t.co/MXgKh8Hjjq — Que Du Foot (@Que_Du_Football) October 26, 2026 In the video, Mbappé is seen holding a microphone as someone applies make-up on his face as questions appear on text on top of the video in French. The first question is about his favorite artist at the moment, and he answers, also in French. Then, he gets asked to choose his favorite meme. "Um, I think the one with Thierry Henry, you know, when he’s smiling," he answers, "that one’s pretty good, because you can use it in so many different ways." Mbappé then tries to replicate Henry's smile in said meme. Then, the clip gets to the new controversial answer, where Mbappé gets asked what meme with his face made him laugh the most. "Well, there are tons of them," he says. "The one that made me laugh the most was when someone took a video of a guy. I think it was a Chinese dictator. And they added my face to it." As he speaks, the video shows a GIF where Mbappé's face was edited onto the head and body of Mao Zedong, who founded the People’s Republic of China and ruled it for over three decades. A portion of the Soviet communist flag can be seen in the background. "I use it a lot with my friends online, you know, while playing on the PlayStation," Mbappé says. item.title: Gasperini analyzes win over Cagliari: “It wasn’t easy, we had several banged-up players.”
item.description: Gasperini analyzes win over Cagliari: “It wasn’t easy, we had several banged-up players.” Gian Piero Gasperini spoke to DAZN after Roma-Cagliari (4-2). The Giallorossi coach commented on his team’s victory: “It’s going very well. We undoubtedly had some players struggling who hadn’t fully recovered. It’s also clear that some of their new players created problems for us. That was the only reason. We always played with the same players in midfield and we saw some signs of fatigue, so it’s even more creditable that we won. Especially at 1-0, we had excellent control, and then also at the end.” The Roma coach on Ghilardi: “He’s had excellent games. He probably should have come on earlier, but then there were situations where it was difficult to make that substitution, otherwise he would have been the first one after half-time. He’s improved a lot compared to last year and will continue to find more space.” Gasperini on the conditions of Balerdi and Hermoso and the absentees: “Balerdi and Hermoso weren’t fit to play. It’s not easy to play so many games without Dybala, Koné, and others. Cristante returned after a month and played two 90-minute games in three days. The win against Cagliari is a great achievement, as they are a tough team to face.” Gian Piero Gasperini spoke about Gollini: “He was a goalkeeper who even played in the Champions League and achieved important goals. At the time, he was younger and more exuberant, less motivated to work and improve. We met again in Rome, and I never had any doubts about his qualities. He trains very well, and I’m happy with what he’s done in recent matches. He’s extraordinary up close, but he concedes goals from distance, but he’s an excellent goalkeeper.” The Giallorossi coach on Lulli and Pisilli: “They’re extraordinary guys. I have to say that there’s always something great going on in the youth academy. There are some guys who are very attached to Roma, and this leads them to dream of making their first-team debuts, and that’s a very positive thing. They’re absolutely talented guys.
